Hi Alyssa / Chris,

Quick one to align on the insurance checklist for the SkyCloud order (DEAL-4821). We hit two items in procurement that need confirmation before I can move the order form to signature:

- Additional Insured (AI): SkyCloud requests AI on Redwood's commercial general liability and auto policies. They have asked for two naming variants: "SkyCloud AI, Inc." and "SkyCloud Technologies LLC". Can you confirm whether the carrier will issue an AI endorsement covering both name variants (or advise the preferred language)?
- Waiver of subrogation: SkyCloud is asking for a waiver in favor of the customer. Please confirm if this is available and whether it requires an endorsement on each policy.
- Aggregate limits and policy period: procurement wants verification that the GL aggregate meets the 2M minimum for the term and evidence of continuous coverage back six months.

Attached is the current draft_orderform_redline.pdf showing the clause SkyCloud flagged as an exception. Aditya — looping you in for legal language options on the MSA/order form if we need to propose alternative wording to procurement.

Ideal timeline from SkyCloud: they want COIs + endorsements prior to countersignature. Can your team provide a target delivery date? If the carrier needs extra lead time, tell us how much and we can propose a short-term interim acknowledgement for signature.

Thanks — Jordan

Hi Jordan / Chris,

Thanks for the details. Quick answers from the broker side:

- Additional Insured naming: we can provide an endorsement that names multiple variants, but carriers prefer a single canonical name where possible. Recommended endorsement line: ""SkyCloud AI, Inc., including subsidiaries and affiliates as identified in writing"" — this generally satisfies most procurement teams and avoids multiple named-entity endorsements. If SkyCloud insists on both exact legal names, we can request both; it may take an extra 48-72 hours for underwriter sign-off.
- Waiver of subrogation: available on GL and auto with carrier approval. Binders can be issued while endorsement is being processed; endorsement issuance typically takes 3-5 business days from request.
- Evidence of continuous coverage: we can pull a past six-month history and include the current declarations page on the COI.

I attached a mercantile-sample-endorsement.pdf showing the proposed AI language and a DocuSign sample link for rapid signature by the insured. If you want the carrier to name both variants precisely, confirm and I’ll submit the formal endorsement request (ETA 3 business days). Otherwise I recommend the canonical name approach for speed.

Proposed delivery schedule: COI + binder within 48 hours if we proceed with canonical name; full endorsement in up to 5 business days.

Best,
Alyssa

Jordan / team,

Thanks for pulling this together. From a legal standpoint we should do two things in parallel:

1) Offer a compromise redline for the Order Form language that limits the exposure while meeting SkyCloud’s procurement requirements. Suggested clause (for insert into Order Form / MSA insurance section):

"Provider shall maintain Commercial General Liability with limits not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate; Automobile Liability with limits of $1,000,000; and Employers' Liability of $500,000. Provider shall add Customer as an Additional Insured on the CGL and Auto policies to the extent required by written contract between the parties, and shall provide a waiver of subrogation to Customer where permitted by law and insurer policy. Evidence of current coverage (COI and declaration page) shall be delivered prior to countersignature. Any endorsement requested to name multiple legal entities must be requested in writing and is subject to carrier approval."
2) To speed procurement, ask Alyssa to issue a COI and binder using the canonical name approach (Alyssa’s recommended text). We can accept the binder/COI for countersignature and track the formal endorsement as a post-signature deliverable with a defined ETA (e.g., 5 business days). Please capture that commitment in the order form as a post-signature deliverable if SkyCloud will accept it.

I’m attaching a short snippet (insurance_redline_snippet.txt) with the above wording formatted for legal review. If procurement pushes for both exact legal names, we should escalate to Ops to confirm if adding those variants materially changes carrier pricing or underwriting — that’s usually the blocker.

Aditya
